A system swings with its largest amplitude when the push's frequency equals its natural frequency: with light damping the largest steady swing on the drive slider sits at the natural frequency, the square root of k ÷ m, and the true top of the hill lies within two percent of it

Resonance can still occur with more damping, but the amplitude at resonance is reduced: each step up in damping, from the lightest to just below where the hill goes, lowers the swing at the natural frequency and the top of the hill, and every one of them still has a top
